ambiguities.description: The Student-enrolls-in-CourseOffering relationship is mentioned but never given explicit cardinality or optionality constraints (e.g., can a student enroll in the same offering multiple times? Is enrollment mandatory for all students? Can an offering have zero enrolled students?). Should uniqueness/mandatory constraints be added for this fact type?

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: The maximum capacity of an offering is described as 'a cap on how many students can enroll' -- is this enforced as a hard constraint (frequency/count) on the Student-enrolls-in-CourseOffering fact type, or just a stored attribute with no automated enforcement?

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether an Instructor can teach the same course offering that another instructor also teaches (co-teaching), or whether an offering must have exactly one instructor always, with no exceptions or historical instructor changes tracked.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between an instructor and offerings mentions 'An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester' -- this seems to just describe non-uniqueness on the Instructor side, but it's unclear if there's any limit intended (e.g., max number of offerings per instructor per semester).

source_references.excerpt: An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Course credit value is described as 'usually between 1 and 6' -- is this a hard, enforced constraint (value range) or just a typical guideline that could have exceptions? The word 'usually' suggests it may not be a strict business rule.

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.

ambiguities.description: The grade fact type ('Student receives LetterGrade for CourseOffering') is derived from/dependent on the enrollment fact ('Student enrolls in CourseOffering') at the end of a semester -- is grade a time-dependent attribute that should track when it was assigned, and is it guaranteed every enrolled student eventually gets a grade (mandatory), or can enrollments remain ungraded (e.g., withdrawal)?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.
